turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I was wondering if you could tell me what brought you in?

turns.text: OK, I see when uh did these symptoms start exactly?

turns.text: OK. Uh, and uh, in terms of the headache, uh, does your head hurt in any particular location?

turns.text: I would say mostly the sides of my head.

turns.text: OK, and how long has the headache been going on for?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh the same amount of time, so like the past three days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and um, how would you describe the headache? Is it like sharp, is it like a vice grip? Is it pulsating, pressure like sensation or none of those?

turns.text: It you know it feels crampy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Um, and has there been anything that triggered the headache or or made it worse?

turns.text: I don't think so. Nothing is helping, sleeping is not helping, moving around is not helping. It's just always there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, does the headache get worse with lying flat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I wouldn't say so, no.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, would you say that this headache, which is was like worst headache of your life or thunder clap kind of sensation?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had headaches like this before in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, never.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, how would you rate it in terms of severity, with 10 being the most severe that you could possibly have and one being not painful at all? How would you rate it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say I would give it around a 6 or seven.

turns.text: OK. And have you had any nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Patient

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, and so you you mentioned that you had you had a fever as well. Did you check your temperature?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I didn't actually, no I didn't check my temperature, I just feel hot.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, we'll be sure to check that today in clinic. And have you been experiencing any other symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, just like the brain fog that I was speaking of, you know. I just don't remember, I remember things, but it's it's like I'm doing everything underwater.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Oh OK. Have you been uh confused or concerns with your memory?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no, I haven't forgotten things. It just feels like I'm really slow at doing things.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, OK, and how has your energy been? Have you had uh significant fatigue?

turns.label: Patient

turns.label: Clinician

turns.text: OK. So I think that was, uh, all of the questions that I wanted to ask on history today. Was there anything else that you thought I was missing or that you wanted to tell me about?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So with the acuity of your symptoms, starting with the last few days and getting worse, especially with a fever which we now have documented of 38.8 and a kind of feeling, uh, tired with aches and pains and the headache, I am concerned that you have possibly a viral infection, and one of those possibilities could be COVID-19, but also it could be the influenza. It could be something like the common cold, such as adenovirus. So certainly we will do a PCR COVID swab as well as order some general lab work to look for signs of infection, such as a CBC and a white blood cell count. But um, for now we will get those tests ordered. Did you have any questions?
